Q14: My biggest takeaway was that paying attention to accessibility needs can require a lot of creativity and resourcefulness, but when effort is put in it can help not only the health and safety of individuals who identify as disabled, but benefit the whole group’s wellbeing. Further, it can improve the science itself. For example, our group devised a plan where students could compare edge effects by having a group in a car getting out to look at species diversity vs inside a field, and students could self assign themselves to groups to avoid the need of disclosure. This idea built around accessibility needs actually resulted in a more nuanced scientific approach as opposed to everyone sampling inside the field.
